subject: Medivex capacity uplift amendment + SOW alignment
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@medivex.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medivex Procurement <procure@medivex.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: capacity uplift + SOW clarifications

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the walk-through yesterday. We ran this by the engineering and procurement teams overnight and they asked for a formal change request so we can process budget approval. High-level ask:

- Add 40 reserved GPU nodes for Phase 2 (Q4 ramp)
- Amend Exhibit C to clarify integration support window (SOW section 2.3)
- Update pricing for burst credits during onboarding month

I've attached our internal change request (Medivex-Change-Request-v1.pdf) with context and an initial preferred effective date of 2026-11-01. Can Redwood produce a proposed change order and a redline to the Order Form / Exhibit C to circulate to our procurement and legal (cc'd)?

Budget owner is Priya Malhotra (procure@medivex.com) — procurement will own signoff once legal signs off on SOW language.

Thanks,
Sophie Lang
Head of AI Platform
Medivex Therapeutics

Attachment: Medivex-Change-Request-v1.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@medivex.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: capacity uplift + SOW clarifications

Hi Sophie —

Appreciate the clear ask and the timeline. We're happy to action this. Next steps from our side:

1) I'll draft a change order that captures the +40 reserved GPU nodes, with two pricing options (monthly commit vs one-time ramp fee) so procurement can pick the preferred path.
2) Laura (cc) will prepare an MSA/Order Form redline to reflect the Exhibit C SOW edits you called out and flag any downstream billing impacts.
3) We will include a targeted DocuSign packet and a tracked-changes Order Form so your legal/finance teams can expedite.

Question: do you have a firm requirement for an SLA tweak on availability for Phase 2, or will the standard Dedicated SLA suffice? If you need a higher SLA lane we'll add that as an optional line item.

I'll attach the draft change order for internal review and aim to send a first-pass redline by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: capacity uplift + SOW clarifications

Thanks Mateo —

Standard Dedicated SLA is fine for now; we don't need a custom SLA lane. Procurement is comfortable evaluating the two pricing options. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Integration window language: we want a dedicated 6-week support window post-go-live for the initial onboarding (clarify responsibilities and acceptance criteria).
- Burst credits: prefer a cap on unanticipated burst spend (a not-to-exceed monthly threshold) and a mechanism for emergency overages to be pre-approved.

I've looped in Anna from Whitecap Law so she can review redlines from a legal standpoint once you send them. Our target is to have commercial and legal agreed by 10/07 so procurement can issue the PO on 10/08.

Sophie

Thanks for the detail and timeline. I'm the contracts lead covering this region — looping in Laura for implementation estimates and Mateo who owns the commercial.

What I'm sending here:

  * Two pricing options included (monthly commit vs one-time ramp charge).
